focus: Phase 2 entry/exit flow: DungeonEntry.Enter caravan split + map generation, DungeonExit as a MapPortal leading to its own cell (deferred move-out, proxy to stash), DungeonSite map removal and IThingHolder re-implementation, the ChoicesAtFor/Caravan.GetGizmos patches
diffSource: since build 6 (2026-10-07T02:32:14Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: DungeonSite still offers vanilla's generic Enter, which drops a second caravan into the walls
findings.detail: DungeonSite.GetFloatMenuOptions starts by calling base (MapParent). MapParent adds CaravanArrivalAction_Enter options whenever UseGenericEnterMapFloatMenuOption is true, and CaravanArrivalAction_Enter.CanEnter only checks HasMap. So while a party is inside, any caravan sees a working vanilla 'Enter' next to the mod's greyed-out 'Enter dungeon (party inside)'. It enters from the map edge, and the placeholder map is solid wall on every edge, so FindNearEdgeCell logs 'Could not find any valid edge cell' and falls back to CellFinder.RandomCell. Pawns can be spawned inside walls, with no party-size or already-entered check. Fix with one line in DungeonSite: `protected override bool UseGenericEnterMapFloatMenuOption => false;`.

findings.title: Enter dialog shows one party wealth and effective level, but the dungeon is built from another
findings.detail: When nobody able stays outside (the 'everyone' case), SelectionChanged and DoInfo work out wealth and the effective level from `going` = caravan.PawnsListForReading. The dialog shows that number and calls it the level the dungeon is generated for. TryAccept then calls DungeonEntry.Enter(caravan, party, ...) with only the ticked `party`. Enter takes `wealth = PartyWealth(party)` before it swaps in everyone, so site.effectiveLevel and the letter leave out the unticked pawns who go in anyway, and the player gets a different level from the one they agreed to. At line 190, pass `(everyone ? caravan.PawnsListForReading : party).ToList()`. Use a copy, not the live list, because Enter removes pawns from the caravan.

findings.title: A DungeonSite with no map blocks its tile for good
findings.detail: Enter adds the site to the world before MapGenerator.GenerateMap. MapParent.CheckRemoveMapNow does nothing when there is no map, and CanEnterAt rejects any tile with a site on it ('party inside'). If map generation throws, or the site ends up without a map some other way, that dungeon can never be entered again. In CanEnterAt, treat (or Destroy) a SiteAt(tile) whose HasMap is false.

findings.title: A drafted pawn leaving through the exit loses the item it carries
findings.detail: JobDriver_EnterPortal only drops a carried item when the pawn is not drafted, and it re-drafts pawns that were drafted. TryMovePawnOut then calls Caravan.AddPawn, which only removes carried pawns, and Pawn.ExitMap destroys any carried item that is not a pawn. In TryMovePawnOut, move carryTracker.CarriedThing into the pawn's inventory (or the stash) before AddPawn.

findings.title: Player animals waiting at the exit can be lost when the map is removed
findings.detail: TryMovePawnOut returns false for an animal when no caravan is outside, so the animal waits in DungeonExit.arrived. When the last colonist leaves, MapParent.TickInterval -> CheckRemoveMapNow can remove the map before DungeonExit.Tick hands the animal to the new caravan, because ShouldRemoveMapNow ignores animals. In DungeonSite.Notify_MyMapAboutToBeRemoved, move still-spawned player pawns from the exit's arrived list out to the waiting caravan.

findings.title: In the 'everyone' case, food and medicine stay outside unless the player ticks them
findings.detail: TransferableOneWay counts start at 0, and in the everyone branch DungeonEntry.Enter stashes `total - CountToTransfer` of each item. If the player never opens the Items or Travel supplies tab, every item, including food and medicine, goes to the stash and the party goes in with nothing. That matches vanilla's split-caravan default, but the TUBAD_Enter_Everyone warning does not mention it. This is my opinion of the UX, not a bug.

findings.title: Static tickedWorld keeps the previous game's World alive
findings.detail: The fix clears the ticked pawns when the finder opens in a new game, but `tickedWorld` is itself a static strong reference to the old World. That World holds its world objects and pawns. After a load, the old game stays in memory until the finder is next opened. A static field can't be avoided here, but clearing it from a GameComponent's FinalizeInit, or holding the world's unique id instead of the object, would let the old game be freed at load time.

findings.title: Placeholder roof counts as overhead mountain
findings.detail: Every cell is roofed with RoofRockThick, which probably makes the dungeon map a target for infestations. Thin roof would avoid that until phase 3 replaces this GenStep.

findings.title: Comment on the PlanetTile ChoicesAtFor postfix names the wrong caller
findings.detail: Patches.cs says the tile overload is 'used to revalidate an open menu'. FloatMenuWorld revalidates through the Vector2 overload (FloatMenuWorld.cs:28, :76, :95), which the other postfix already covers. The only vanilla caller of the tile overload is CaravanExitMapUtility:77, which runs the first enabled option for a destination chosen while forming a caravan. So a caravan formed with a dungeon tile as its destination gets the enter order automatically, unless an earlier option on that tile wins (ours is appended last). The behaviour is fine; correct the comment so nobody 'fixes' the wrong patch later.

findings.title: wealthToDouble slider range is narrower than the range the settings file allows
findings.detail: DungeonSettings clamps a loaded value to 1000..1000000, but the Parties tab slider runs 5000..300000. A hand-edited or older value outside 5000..300000 is replaced with the slider bound as soon as the tab is opened. Either match the slider bounds to the clamp, or tighten the clamp to the slider.

findings.title: verify_patches' MethodType.Enumerator advice for Caravan.GetGizmos does not apply
findings.detail: The postfix takes and returns IEnumerable<Gizmo> and yields the original gizmos first. Harmony runs that as a pass-through postfix, so the added command is enumerated as expected and the vanilla gizmos are kept. No corpus mod patches Caravan.GetGizmos or Pawn.GetGizmos, so there is no precedent to compare against. Leave it as is.
